title: Order items persist client-supplied UnitPrice/Discount/Units with no server-side price verification
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/
rationale: Adds the missing aggregate invariants to the OrderItem constructor (throw on unitPrice <= 0 and discount < 0, before the existing discount-vs-total check) and mirrors them as a FluentValidation rule on CreateOrderCommand so failures surface as clean 400s. Closing the GetTotal manipulation for every caller including the draft endpoint. KNOWN LIMITATION (stated): this blocks negative/zero/garbage prices but not underpricing — true price authority requires a Catalog lookup, which Ordering.API cannot wire without a new gRPC client (recommended follow-up).
variants_checked: Only two production OrderItem construction sites (create handler, draft handler), both funnel through the fixed constructor; no catalog/grpc client exists in Ordering.API; SetNewDiscount already rejected negative discounts.
bypass_considered: Negative price, zero price, negative discount all blocked at two layers; underpricing (0.01 vs catalog 500) still passes — honestly noted, requires the catalog-lookup follow-up.
test_note: Four new cases in tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Domain/OrderAggregateTest.cs (zero price, negative price, negative discount, aggregate AddOrderItem path).
review_reason: Root-cause fix at the DDD layer the codebase's own comments assign invariants to, covering both handlers via the constructor; validator mirrors it for clean 400s; tests use existing builders/idioms.
